items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: Well, Johnny was always the very strong force of the Ellington Orchestra... I'd come over and do the job for him, whether it was playing the lead chair or whether it was playing Johnny's chair or whatever it was.

ctx.x: Tell me about that. You told me that because you had worked with Duke in the past, Duke knew that you could step right in and take over any part (inaudible) there and when Johnny Hodges left in '51, you said Duke called you, right?

Well, Johnny was always the very strong force of the Ellington Orchestra and by Johnny leaving, everyone thought that, 'Oh, gee, that's going to put a big hole in the orchestra,' so Duke always sort of held me as an ace in the hole or a card up his sleeve, because he would know that anytime he was in hailing distance of me, all he had to do was call and I'd come over and do the job for him, whether it was playing the lead chair or whether it was playing Johnny's chair or whatever it was.
